title: Node-volume archive creator filters hide retained history after the creator is disabled or logically deleted
correction: Node-volume creator filters resolve retained control-database account identities by organization and public id, matching shared-store historical behavior. The creator target does not need current login eligibility. Authenticated administrator checks, Runtime admission, logical user deletion and retained archive data remain unchanged.

distinctNamedCases.qualification: Archive mutations, administrator read qualification, Runtime namespace and the actual mixed-store Gateway replay. Case identities are distinct.

publicHttpReplay.qualification: A real one-connection governance pool and separate attested content database. Six new scenarios cover active, disabled, logically deleted, organization-membership disabled or removed creators, and absent targets. Real user-service disablement/deletion retains both histories and labels. Existing late actor withdrawal and mixed draft controls stay intact.

ordinaryNodeArtifacts.qualification: Ordinary unchanged Gateway emit with two actual PostgreSQL databases and real node-content attestation on macOS.

lint.qualification: The MJS fixture is ignored by existing lint configuration and executes in source and both ordinary artifact versions.

verificationQualification: An initial local fixture assertion used creatorUserId instead of the documented creator.id. It was corrected before the definitive19-scenario counterproof, which isolates only the two inactive-creator failures. Both earlier runs remain in external evidence. No production change was inferred from the fixture field error.

noteReview.reason: The existing decision owns logical removal and retained historical references. Creator filtering uses that same historical identity without changing current actor qualification or promising transcript survival after project deletion.

additionalSourceReview.retentionBatchLimit: The mixed-store purgeDue limit currently applies independently to each store. Aggregate versus per-store semantics and retention fairness are not established as a defect; no production change or new finding is claimed.
additionalSourceReview.search: Repository search and current query consumers remain under review. Source inspection alone does not establish a current product access bug or complete the search domain.

limits: All12business domains remain in progress. Three measured compiled lookup ranges execute in each ordinary Node version; no whole-method, whole-file or whole-project100percent claim.
Remaining archive/search, resource/helper allocation and native-platform review stays open. Peer implementation and production deployment are unchanged.
